builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution
summary: TESD replaces standard On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), which uses a static self-teacher, by adding teacher-oriented optimization and adaptive student weighting based on reward feedback. It costs additional rollouts and environmental feedback for teacher training, increasing computational overhead and implementation complexity compared to vanilla OPSD. The method can fail if reward signals are noisy or unreliable, leading to incorrect reliability estimates and suboptimal teacher evolution.
rationale: While promising for improving post-training quality on constrained infrastructure, the method requires additional rollouts and feedback mechanisms that increase cost and complexity, necessitating small-scale validation before production adoption.

claims.statement: TESD replaces standard On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), which uses a static self-teacher, by adding teacher-oriented optimization and adaptive student weighting based on reward feedback. It costs additional rollouts and environmental feedback for teacher training, increasing computational overhead and implementation complexity compared to vanilla OPSD. The method can fail if reward signals are noisy or unreliable, leading to incorrect reliability estimates and suboptimal teacher evolution.
TESD consistently outperforms representative token-level and sequence-level methods across multiple datasets and model scales.
